# Emitted-size baseline for the SELF-HOSTED compiler over examples/bench,
# checked against every run by scripts/ci-check-perf.
#
# FORMAT: metric  value  [tolerance%]. The metric key is
# selfhost/<target>/<benchmark>.emit — indented lines of emitted output, which
# is one per machine instruction for the two native targets and one per WAT
# s-expression body line for wasm32-wasi. See scripts/perf-bench-selfhost for
# why this is `.emit` and not the native lane's `.text`: they do not measure
# the same thing and should not share a name.
#
# EXACT. Every figure here is a property of the emitted text for a given commit
# and repeats byte-for-byte across runs and hosts — verified over three
# consecutive runs when the lane landed. There is no noise floor, so the
# comparator's 1% default is a significance threshold and no entry needs its
# own tolerance. That is the whole reason the lane measures emitted size rather
# than anything timed.
#
# WHY THIS FILE IS SEPARATE FROM perf-baseline.txt. That one measures the
# NATIVE compiler and is namespaced by HOST arch, because its dynamic half has
# to execute. This lane is namespaced by TARGET: one self-host binary
# cross-emits all three, so both CI hosts produce these same numbers, and a
# divergence between hosts is itself a defect this file would catch.
#
# THREE TARGETS, COMPARED SIDE BY SIDE. The point is not the absolute figures
# but the ratios between targets on the same program. arm64 drifting away from
# x86-64 is what an unconditionally-emitted runtime bundle looks like — that is
# exactly how arm64 came to carry ~400 instructions of f64 transcendental
# runtime in every program, including pure-integer ones, until #2649 gated it
# (int_loop: 468 -> 62). Two keys moving apart is the signal.
#
# ADVISORY, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS — see scripts/ci-check-perf. When a number moves
# on purpose, update it in the same PR; the job summary prints the corrected
# lines ready to paste. Keep the reason in the PR, not here.
